features: A full-width consumer unit with seven breakers (fault finding, fuse board, EV charger, rewire, EICR, sockets and lights, emergency); flip one and it switches on to show what is included, the price and a button to ring
The main switch is the phone number, and every number on the page swaps between the office line and the emergency mobile from the London clock
The circuit chart beside the board is the price list: tap a row and its breaker flips on
Real photos, a three-field call-back, a postcode check across NG1 to NG17, and a sticky Call and Quote bar on phones
name: Kestrel Electrical
short: An electrician's page built as a fuse board: every job is a breaker.
long: Real photos, the phone number at poster size and a three-field call-back up top. The services are a full-width consumer unit: flip a breaker and it switches on to show what's included, what it costs and a button to ring about it. The circuit chart beside it is the price list. The only things that move are switches.
proves: Someone standing in a dark kitchen can ring the right number in one tap, at any hour, without reading a word of marketing.
story: Most trade sites bury the number under a hero image and a form nobody fills in. Borrowing the layout of the thing an electrician opens every day made the page label itself: everything is a switch, and the biggest one rings the phone.
